title: Warm KV cache starvation and priority shedding playbook
creator: Ava Chen
summary: During a sustained increase in priority traffic to a single region, warm KV caches became starved for critical prefixes which amplified tail latency and triggered cascading priority-based load shedding across secondary regions. This incident caused ~6% latency SLO misses and transient 15% request drop rate for P0 customers in the affected availability zone for ~45 minutes.
impact: Latency SLO (p99) elevated by 40-120ms for affected routes; ~6% of requests returned rate-limited errors for P0/P1 customers in region-eu-west for 00:45. No data loss; errors were predominantly 429/503 from circuit-breaker-driven shedding.
detection: Automated SLO alert (p99 > 350ms) triggered at 2026-03-10T10:13Z. Runbook alerted on-call. Console trace showed rising KV miss rate and queue depth growth on serving tier. Secondary-region circuit breakers started opening at 10:18Z.
timeline: 10:10Z - Slight traffic skew observed toward eu-west; normal retention of KV shards expected to absorb
10:12Z - KV cache hit-rate began a steady decline for popular prefixes (tokenization metadata).
10:15Z - On-call ingested metrics; initial mitigations attempted: scaled pool by 2x in eu-west, warmed a subset of cold keys (manual script).

10:18Z - Circuit breakers in other regions tripped to protect capacity; priority-based shedding policy started dropping low-priority requests but misapplied to some higher-priority routes due to label mismatch.
10:30Z - Emergency KV prefetch job ran, warming top-100 prefixes; visible improvement in hit rate but residual queueing remained.
10:58Z - All circuit breakers gradually closed as backlog drained and hit-rate recovered. Incident declared mitigated at 10:58Z.
11:00Z - Post-incident triage session scheduled; deep-dive assigned.
11:45Z - Blameless postmortem draft created and circulated for review.
root_cause: A combination of an unanticipated sustained high-volume traffic skew to a small set of prefixes, conservative KV cache eviction policies tuned for steady-state rather than bursty hot-prefix patterns, and an overly-broad priority label matching rule caused automated shedding to misclassify some higher-priority requests. This exposed a coupling between cache warming, KV miss amplification, and heterogeneous circuit-breaker thresholds across regions.
contributing_factors: KV eviction policy uses recency only; no hot-prefix weight for bursty access
Cold-start warming only runs on new model deployments, not on sudden hot-prefix surges
Circuit-breaker thresholds tuned independently per region without cross-region coordination
Priority label schema mismatch: a new internal route used legacy label that matched lower-priority shedding rule
Insufficient observability for per-prefix miss growth; alerts are per-service rather than per-prefix
immediate_mitigations: Scaled serving pool in eu-west to absorb spike (manual autoscale override)
Ran emergency prefetch/warm job for top-100 observed prefixes
Applied temporary override to shedding rules to exclude the mis-labeled route
Rotated circuit-breaker hysteresis to more conservative close thresholds to avoid oscillation
long_term_actions: Implement hot-prefix scoring in KV eviction (weight by short-term QPS and moving-window hits) - owner: Priya Kapoor - due: 2026-04-15
Add adaptive warmers: background prefetch jobs triggered by rapid prefix QPS increases - owner: Liam O'Connor - due: 2026-04-30
Unify priority label canonicalization in the routing surface and add CI checks to prevent mismatches - owner: Diego Morales - due: 2026-03-28
Introduce per-prefix alerting heuristics and dashboards (top-200 prefixes by traffic) - owner: Analytics team (linked) - due: 2026-04-10
Coordinate circuit-breaker policy rollout: introduce cross-region hysteresis policy with simulated replay testing before prod changes - owner: Runtime Reliability - due: 2026-05-01
Add graceful degradation flow that prefers shedding synthetic/low-cost tokens first rather than whole-request drops - owner: Product & Runtime - due: 2026-05-15
notes: Triage and mitigation were broadly effective, but the incident highlighted several brittle coupling points between caching, routing labels, and multi-region CB policies. We prioritized non-invasive mitigations during the incident; long-term fixes require cross-team coordination. We'll run a chaos test in a staging ring to validate hot-prefix warmers and cross-region CB hysteresis by 2026-04-20.
retrospective_decision_log: Do not change global shedding thresholds mid-incident unless clear per-route mapping is verified
Invest in lightweight per-prefix tracing in the runtime to make detection and automated warming feasible
Treat priority label canonicalization as a breaking change candidate with CI gates
